description: The bar chart illustrates the number of morphosyntactic probing tasks performed across various language families in the context of evaluating multilingual BERT models, as presented in the paper “Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models.” The horizontal axis, labeled “# tasks,” ranges from 0 to 80 in increments of 10, representing the count of probing tasks per language family. The vertical axis lists language families in descending order of task count: an unlabeled top category (light gray, ~79 tasks), followed by IE-Romance (dark blue, ~47 tasks), IE-Germanic (light green, ~44 tasks), Uralic (green, ~20 tasks), IE-Baltic (pink, ~17 tasks), IE-other (red, ~15 tasks), IE-Indic (beige, ~10 tasks), Semitic (orange, ~8 tasks), Turkic (lavender, ~5 tasks), and Basque (purple, ~3 tasks). Each bar’s length corresponds to the number of tasks, with the top unlabeled category having the longest bar and Basque the shortest. The chart uses distinct colors for each language family, and no grouping or stacking is present — each bar represents a single category. The bars are sorted in descending order of task count, visually emphasizing the disparity in probing coverage across language families.
